question: Announced in 2025, in which state is Similipal National Park located?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Odisha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Similipal National Park** is located in the **Mayurbhanj** district of the Indian state of **Odisha**. It is one of the largest national parks in India, spanning an area of approximately **2,750 square kilometers**.
 
• The name of the park is derived from the abundance of **Simul** (Red Silk Cotton) trees that bloom vividly in the region, contributing to its unique ecosystem.
 
• It was formally designated as a **Tiger Reserve** under **Project Tiger** in the year **1973**. The area was earlier a hunting ground for the royalty of **Mayurbhanj**.
 
• The government declared it a **Wildlife Sanctuary** in **1979** and subsequently a **National Park** in **1980**. It serves as a vital habitat for the **Bengal Tiger** and the **Asian Elephant**.
 
• Similipal is world-renowned for being the only natural habitat of the **Melanistic Tiger** (Black Tiger), characterized by thick black stripes due to genetic mutations. ***Hence, the correct answer is Odisha.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **UNESCO Recognition**:
 
 
• In **1994**, the Government of India declared Similipal a **Biosphere Reserve**.
 
• It was added to the **UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves** in May **2009**, recognizing its global ecological significance and biodiversity.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Features**:
 
 
• The park is home to some of India's most breathtaking waterfalls, including **Barehipani Falls**, which has a height of **399 meters**, and **Joranda Falls**.
 
• The terrain is characterized by high plateaus and hills, with the highest peak being **Khairiburu**, standing at an elevation of about **1,178 meters**.
 
• Several perennial rivers originate from these hills, such as the **Budhabalanga**, **Salandi**, and the **Palpala** rivers.
 
 
 
• **Flora and Fauna**:
 
 
• The park's vegetation is a rich mosaic of **Northern Tropical Moist Deciduous Forests** and **Semi-Evergreen Forests**.
 
• It boasts over **1,000 species** of plants and **96 species** of orchids. The wildlife includes **Gaur** (Indian Bison), **Chausingha** (Four-horned Antelope), **Leopard**, and over **300 species of birds** such as the **Hill Myna**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Tribal Inhabitants**: The region is inhabited by several indigenous tribes, including the **Kolha**, **Santhal**, **Bhumija**, and **Mankidia**. These communities have a deep cultural and symbiotic relationship with the forest.
 
• **Conservation Efforts**: The **Mayurbhanj Elephant Reserve** includes the Similipal-Hadgarh-Kuldiha forests, forming a massive conservation landscape for **elephants** in Eastern India.
 
• **Environmental Concerns**: The park frequently faces threats from **forest fires** during the summer months (February to June) and issues related to **poaching**, which the state government of **Odisha** manages through specialized forest protection squads.
 
• **Tourism**: Entry to the park is usually regulated and remains closed during the **monsoon season** (June to October) to ensure visitor safety and allow for wildlife breeding.
